title: Floquet ground state order
authors: Suman Mondal, Paul M. Schindler, Marin Bukov
abstract: Clean, interacting, periodically driven systems are believed to thermalize to featureless, infinite-temperature states that preclude the formation of stable ordered states. Here, we show stable quantum order, distinct from prethermal order, and its phase transitions in the ground state of the average-energy operator. Decomposing the time evolution into geometric and average-energy dynamics, we apply Geometric Floquet theory to identify the Floquet ground state. We derive a general variational principle to compute the Floquet ground state in large interacting periodically driven systems, and use it to develop a matrix product state algorithm. In driven nonintegrable chains of more than 100 interacting spins, our numerical simulations exhibit a gapped, area-law entangled Floquet ground state in extended parameter regimes; the ground-state manifold can support both dressed equilibrium order (e.g., Floquet antiferromagnets) and inherently nonequilibrium order (e.g., ground-state time crystals). This quantum order is protected by a finite average-energy gap, which closes at phase transition points upon changing model parameters. We decompose Floquet phases of matter into their equilibrium and nonequilibrium elements: whereas the Floquet ground state at any fixed time is a representative of an equilibrium phase of matter, the nonequilibrium content is entirely produced by the drive holonomy and is geometric. Finally, we identify quasilocal counterdiabatic driving as a mechanism for the stability against heating of gapped Floquet ground states in nonintegrable quantum systems, and argue why Floquet ground states evade the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis. Our work enables the study of interacting nonequilibrium matter deep into the many-body regime, and lays the foundations for the engineering of strongly correlated ordered quantum states.
summary: This paper establishes the existence of stable, ordered quantum states in periodically driven (Floquet) interacting systems, contradicting simple thermalization expectations. By using Geometric Floquet theory, the authors identify the order via the average-energy ground state, showing this order is protected by a finite energy gap. This work provides foundational tools for engineering strongly correlated, non-equilibrium quantum matter.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical challenge of demonstrating stable quantum order in clean, interacting, periodically driven (Floquet) systems, contrasting this with expected thermalization to featureless states.
main_result: Stable quantum order, distinct from prethermal order, is shown to exist in nonintegrable, periodically driven spin chains, protected by a finite average-energy gap.
method: The authors employ Geometric Floquet theory (GFT) and derive a variational principle to compute the Floquet ground state, which is then analyzed using Matrix Product State (MPS) algorithms.
model_or_system: The study focuses on clean, interacting, periodically driven quantum spin chains (Floquet systems). The dynamics are decomposed into geometric and average-energy components, allowing the identification of the Floquet ground state via the average-energy operator.
key_observables: Average-energy gap, entanglement entropy (area-law scaling), and the detection of different order types (e.g., Floquet antiferromagnets, time crystals).
important_parameters: The drive period ($T$), the system size ($L>100$), and the gap magnitude, which closes at phase transition points.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes clean (disorder-free) systems and relies on the existence of a finite average-energy gap to protect the ordered state against heating.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the decomposition of time evolution into geometric and average-energy dynamics, showing the persistence of a gapped, weakly-entangled ground state across varying driving periods.
paper_structure: The paper introduces GFT to decompose the time evolution, derives a variational principle for the average-energy ground state, applies this to 1D spin chains using MPS, and concludes by identifying the gap protection mechanism and the evasion of the ETH.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a rigorous theoretical framework for engineering and characterizing non-equilibrium quantum phases of matter, directly impacting the understanding of driven many-body systems.
